messages.rawText: IMPORTANT NBEMS NOTICE: FMGE December 2026 examination schedule notification announced.

Which of the following is the drug of choice for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT)?
A) Adenosine
B) Amiodarone
C) Verapamil
D) Digoxin
Ans: A
Exp: IV Adenosine is first line.

Observe the clinical video showing rhythmic horizontal eye oscillation. Diagnosis?
A) Horizontal Jerk Nystagmus
B) Opsoclonus
C) Ocular flutter
D) Saccades
Ans: A
Exp: Jerk nystagmus with slow drift.

A 45-year-old male presents with epigastric pain radiating to back. CT abdomen is attached. What is the diagnosis?
A) Acute pancreatitis
B) Peptic ulcer
C) Cholecystitis
D) Appendicitis
Ans: A
Exp: CT demonstrates necrotizing pancreatitis.

Which of the following is the drug of choice for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT)?
A) Adenosine
B) Amiodarone
C) Verapamil
D) Digoxin
Ans: A
Exp: IV Adenosine (6mg rapid bolus) is the first-line drug of choice for acute termination of stable PSVT.

questions.subject: medicine
questions.questionText: Observe the clinical video showing rhythmic horizontal eye oscillation. Diagnosis?

whyOtherOptionsAreWrong.reason: Option B (Opsoclonus) consists of chaotic, multidirectional, rapid involuntary conjugate saccades without an intersaccadic interval, classically linked to pediatric Neuroblastoma or paraneoplastic syndromes.
Option C (Ocular flutter) features purely horizontal back-to-back saccadic oscillations without an intersaccadic interval, lacking the distinct slow drift and fast corrective phase of jerk nystagmus.
Option D (Saccades) are normal high-speed conjugate eye movements that shift foveal fixation from one target to another, not repetitive rhythmic pathological oscillations.

questions.subject: surgery
questions.questionText: A 45-year-old male presents with epigastric pain radiating to back. CT abdomen is attached. What is the diagnosis?

whyOtherOptionsAreWrong.reason: Option B (Peptic ulcer perforation) presents with sudden-onset board-like abdominal rigidity and subdiaphragmatic free air (pneumoperitoneum) on erect chest X-ray, rather than peripancreatic fluid stranding.

Option C (Acute cholecystitis) causes right upper quadrant tenderness with positive Murphy sign, gallbladder wall thickening (>4 mm), and pericholecystic fluid on ultrasound; lipase is typically normal.
Option D (Acute appendicitis) presents with periumbilical pain migrating to McBurney point in the right lower quadrant, accompanied by Rovsing and psoas signs, without elevated serum lipase.

questions.subject: medicine
questions.questionText: Which of the following is the drug of choice for paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT)?
questions.explanation: IV Adenosine (6mg rapid bolus) is the first-line drug of choice for acute termination of stable PSVT.

whyOtherOptionsAreWrong.reason: Option B (Amiodarone) is a Class III antiarrhythmic used primarily for ventricular tachycardia (VT/VF) and atrial fibrillation. Its onset of action is far too slow for acute PSVT termination.

Option C (Verapamil) is a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used as a second-line agent. It is strictly contraindicated in pre-excited AFib (WPW) and heart failure due to negative inotropic depression.

Option D (Digoxin) is a cardiac glycoside with a delayed onset of action (>60-120 minutes) and narrow therapeutic window. It is used for chronic rate control in AFib with heart failure, never for acute PSVT.

pearls.title: Clinical High-Yield Recall
pearls.takeaway: FMGE PEARL: Jerk nystagmus is named after the direction of the fast corrective phase (e.g. right-beating). In peripheral vestibular lesions (e.g. vestibular neuritis), nystagmus beats away from the lesion and is suppressed by visual fixation (Frenzel glasses).

pearls.title: Clinical High-Yield Recall
pearls.takeaway: FMGE PEARL: Serum Lipase is the most sensitive and specific biomarker for acute pancreatitis (remains elevated 8-14 days vs 3-5 days for amylase). Contrast-enhanced CT (CECT) after 72 hours is the gold standard to evaluate pancreatic necrosis (Balthazar score).

pearls.title: Clinical High-Yield Recall
pearls.takeaway: FMGE PEARL: IV Adenosine (6 mg rapid IV push via large antecubital vein followed by 20 mL saline flush; repeat with 12 mg if needed) is the 1st-line drug of choice for acute termination of stable narrow-complex PSVT. It causes transient AV node conduction block (half-life < 10 seconds). Always warn the patient of transient chest pressure and flushing.
